title: CoE/ViPS Invited Seminar October 2026
content:
Date: 7th October 2026

Time: 13:00

Title: Photosynthesis Phenotyping: From Stress Sensing to Mechanisms and Genetics

Location: Seminar room 1015, Biocentre 2, Viikinkaari 5 

Host: Alexey Shapiguzov

Abstract: Improving the resource-use efficiency and resilience of plant photosynthesis is widely regarded as a key strategy in crop breeding to safeguard food security under global climate change. As our understanding of photosynthetic reactions and their regulatory mechanisms has advanced considerably, growing research effort is now directed toward translating this knowledge into applications for agriculture, horticulture, and crop breeding.

In this presentation, I will highlight two recent research focuses of my group related to photosynthesis. The first concerns new methods for analyzing photosynthesis "in action." We use harmonically oscillating light to systematically probe the dynamic responses of photosynthesis and infer the kinetic properties of its regulatory mechanisms. Combined with machine learning, this approach is also being explored for applications in plant stress detection and classification.

title: Webinar Event - Forests for Future: Halting Biodiversity Decline by Restoring Forest Ecosystems
content: Join us on Zoom on November 4, 2026 at 15:00 CEST for the second joint EXTRA/EXALT symposium in collaboration with the TreesForDev research project. Forests are at the front lines of the global climate crisis. In this symposium we explore the still much neglected issue of biodiversity loss and deforestation, sometimes also glossed as ecosystem collapse. Our point of departure is a new pivotal report released by IPBES, the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Biodiversity and Environmental Services, highlighting the economic risks of failing to act on the already dramatic loss of ecosystem health that has been documented. In this symposium we explore the role of afforestation in mitigating biodiversity loss and ecosystem restoration, and in reducing climate change through carbon abatement. We bring together three experts to talk about deforestation, the role of wildfires, afforestation, and how ecological restoration requires more than just tree planting. Our speakers come from the critical social sciences, management and organization studies, and forest policy. Their unique perspectives will support a rich dialogue on what policies will best serve to prevent further forest and biodiversity loss.

title: Ashfak Mahmud will defend his PhD thesis
content:
Ashfak Mahmud will defend his PhD thesis titled "Multisource remote sensing framework for monitoring soil, crop and land-surface processes in smallholder farms"  on Friday, 2 October 2026, at 12:00 at the University of Helsinki.

This dissertation explores remote sensing approaches for monitoring heterogeneous smallholder agricultural systems in East Africa. The research combines observations from proximal hyperspectral sensors, field cameras, UAVs, and satellites to assess soil organic carbon and nitrogen, monitor crop phenology, biophysical traits and agroclimatic responses, and analyse fractional vegetation cover and land surface temperature. The dissertation demonstrates how observations from different platforms and spatial scales can complement each other to provide more timely, detailed, and scalable information for monitoring diverse smallholder agricultural landscapes.

 The study is one of the results of REACT project (Regenerative agricultural systems for climate resilience in agroecological gradient in East Africa) funded by the Research Council of Finland.

Time: Friday, 2 October 2026, 12:00

title: Antti Autio will defend his PhD thesis
content:
Antti Autio will defend his PhD thesis titled "Contextuality and Climate Change Adaptation in Taita Taveta County, Kenya: Negotiating Adaptation across Heterogeneous Agroecological Landscapes"  on Friday, 25 September 2026, at 12:00 at the University of Helsinki. 

This dissertation examines climate change adaptation among smallholder farmers in Taita Taveta County, Kenya, through three empirical studies on climate-smart agriculture, contextual vulnerability, regenerative agriculture, and positive deviance. It explores how adaptation is shaped by agroecological diversity, institutions, markets, gendered vulnerabilities, local knowledge, and farmer agency. The dissertation argues that adaptation is not simply the adoption of externally promoted practices or technologies, but a contextual, negotiated, and relational process emerging from everyday farming decisions within heterogeneous agroecological landscapes.

title: Päivitetyt SSH-alojen aineistonhallinnan (RDM) käsikirjat julkaistu tutkijoiden ja opetuksen tueksi
content:
The SSH Research Data Management Handbooksprovide practical, data-type-specific guidance on research data management for researchers, teachers, and students in the fields of social sciences and humanities.

The handbooks were originally developed as part of the SSH Research Data Management Development Project conducted in 2022–2023. The project and the development of the handbooks are discussed in a Think Open blog post in which Data Support specialists Mikko Ojanen and Maija Paavolainen reflect on their experiences and insights gained during the development process of the handbooks.

“National and institutional guidelines explain what aspects of research data management should be taken into account, but they rarely help researchers solve the data management challenges they encounter in their everyday work,” Ojanen and Paavolainen observe.

title: Erasmus+ Research Stay of Denisa Šárová
content:
Denisa, a visiting Ph.D. researcher from the Faculty of Pharmacy at Charles University, Czech Republic, spent four months at the University of Helsinki as a visiting researcher in the Medicinal Chemistry Research Group. She is also a researcher at the Biomedical Research Centre, University Hospital Hradec Králové, where she began her research activities during her master’s studies.

Her research background is focused on medicinal chemistry and the development of novel FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitors with potential applications in the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia. During her visit to the University of Helsinki, she joined Kiuru research group and contributed to a project focused on the synthesis of aminophosphonates targeting carbonic anhydrases IX and XII as potential anticancer agents.

title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu vuodenvaihteen jälkeen – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Arkadiankadun siltaremontti aiheuttaa muutoksia liikennejärjestelyihin Luonnontieteellisen museon lähistöllä
content:
The renovation will start with the construction of temporary traffic arrangements from Wednesday 7 January onwards. The renovation is expected to be completed in late 2026.

A temporary bridge for pedestrians will be built on the east side of Arkadiankatu over the Baana. The aim is to maintain the pedestrian route on the east side of the bridge until the temporary bridge is operational. Cyclists will also be able to use the bridge.

The Baana route underneath the bridge is expected to remain open for most of the renovation's duration, with some minor exceptions.

There will be changes to the motor vehicle routes by the bridge and around it in January. If possible, should be favoured during the bridge renovation.

Connections to the bus terminals in Kamppi will remain available, but there will be a slight diversion of routes.

Trams 1 and 1T will run via Simonkatu and Kamppi. Lasipalatsi and the Natural History Museum will not be served.

The diversion is due to the renovation of the Arkadiankatu bridge and will remain in place until late 2026. The renovation will not affect HSL's bus services.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Salla Saastamoinen tuo kolmen vuosikymmenen EU-kokemuksen Helsingin yliopistoon
content:
After earning a Licentiate of Laws degree at the University of Helsinki, Salla Saastamoinen worked at the European Commission for more than three decades, advancing from specialist duties to the senior leadership of the Commission. Her latest position was Deputy Director-General of the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF), where she has also served as Acting Director-General. Previously she served in similar positions as Deputy Director-General of the Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) and as Acting Director-General of the Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers. Now she is returning to the University of Helsinki in an entirely new role.

“This feels inspiring and invigorating. I like new beginnings. Even though I’m returning to a familiar place, the University, Helsinki and Finland have surely all changed in the last 30 years that I have spent working in Brussels and the European Commission,” surmises Saastamoinen.

title: Tutkijat löysivät masennukselle viisi erilaista aivoprofiilia
content:
According to the World Health Organization (WHO, 2025), depression affects roughly 332 million (5.2%) adults globally. In Finland, depression is the most common single cause of both prolonged absences due to illness and disability pensions.

Researchers at the University of Helsinki measured brain activity in 263 people with major depressive disorder and 75 healthy control subjects.

The analysis identified five groups where functional connectivity between brain regions differed. This connectivity reflects how effectively the regions function simultaneously, mirroring communication between the regions. 

“What was particularly interesting was the contrasting patterns of brain activity found under the umbrella of the same depression diagnoses. In some individuals, the functional connectivity between brain regions was stronger than usual, while in others it was weaker,” says Director Satu Palva of the Neuroscience Center, University of Helsinki.
